newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's economy slows in November 1996.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's economy slows in November 1996.

text.p: Lebanon's economic activity retreated in November for the third month in a row, the central bank said on Tuesday.
The Bank of Lebanon said in its latest monthly bulletin that its coincident indicator of economic activity dropped to 171.1 in November from 175.9 in October and 176.4 in September.
The indicator -- which takes January 1993 as 100 -- combines 12 economic series including imports, exports, electricity output and airport and port activity.

The central bank created the indicator in 1993 because of a lack of reliable data in Lebanon since the 1975-90 civil war, which prevents precise calculation of gross domestic product (GDP) and economic growth.

The Bank said construction activity continued a slowing trend begun four months ago as cement deliveries dropped to 354,000 tonnes in November from 368,000 tonnes in October, 376,000 tonnes in September and 391,639 tonnes in August.
The construction permits area approved in November by the Association of Engineers declined by 73.3 percent from the levels recorded a year earlier, the Bank said.

Lebanon's trade deficit dropped to $562 million in November from $601 million in October -- bringing the January-November total to $5,886.3 million compared with $5,898.0 million for the same period in 1995.
But the balance of payments recorded a surplus of $221.1 million in November compared with a $141.1 million surplus a month earlier "due to sustained capital inflows that covered the trade deficit".
This brought the BoP surplus for the year to date to $684.6 million against $147 million for the same period in 1995, the central bank added.
Banking activity was up in November, with the consolidated balance sheet of Lebanon's commercial banks registering a rise of 2.9 percent to 35,784 billion Lebanese pounds.

Total deposits in foreign currencies and Lebanese pounds rose 2.78 percent to 29,870 billion pounds from 29,062 billion in October, it said. Lebanese pound deposits grew 3.49 percent to 12,978 billion pounds from 12,541 billion a month earlier.
Loans and credits to the private sector rose 2.43 percent in November over October to 12,480 billion pounds.
Foreign debt rose $43.6 million in November to $1,702.3 million and net total public debt rose 292.5 billion pounds to 15,604.3 billion.
"The increase in debt was mainly due to the rise in net domestic debt which reached 12,957.3 billion pounds at end November," the Bank added.
